skill.name: dependency-sync
skill.description: Detects imports added during implementation and updates matching dependency manifests with the correct package manager.
skill.summary: Keeps dependency manifests aligned with newly added imports across common language ecosystems.
skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from Markdown code fences and package mapping tables. The real risk is the skill design: it installs inferred dependencies by default without prompting, which can introduce unreviewed third-party code. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Automatic dependency installation is enabled without confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Set PROMPT_BEFORE_INSTALL to true by default and require explicit approval before package manager commands run.

remediation.issue: Package names are inferred from imports before installation.
remediation.suggestion: Validate each resolved package against an allowlist or trusted registry metadata, and show the exact package before installation.

remediation.issue: Package managers can run install or build behavior for third-party packages.
remediation.suggestion: Use lockfile-only updates when possible and disable lifecycle scripts where package managers support it.

remediation.issue: Manifest changes may be committed automatically.
remediation.suggestion: Disable automatic commits by default and require a reviewed diff before committing dependency changes.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Third-Party Dependency Installation
semantic_findings.description: The skill enables automatic installation by default and disables prompting by default. It then instructs package manager installs for missing dependencies, which can fetch unreviewed third-party code.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The defaults and workflow directly show unattended installation behavior. Package manager installs are a known supply-chain execution path.

semantic_findings.title: Unreviewed Dependency Name Inference
semantic_findings.description: The skill maps imports to package names and defaults unknown imports to package names. Malicious, misspelled, or ambiguous imports can drive installation of unexpected registry packages.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cookbooks explicitly fall back to package-name assumptions after known mappings. The risk depends on the modified code, so confidence is high but not absolute.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Manifest Commit Behavior
semantic_findings.description: COMMIT_CHANGES defaults to true, and the success report includes a commit reference. This can preserve malicious or mistaken dependency changes before human review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The variable default and example output indicate intended commit behavior. The exact commit command is not shown, so confidence is below very high.

content.value_statement: New imports often fail builds when manifests are not updated. This skill detects added imports and helps install or record the matching packages.
actual_capabilities: Detects modified Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go, and Rust files from implementation context or git diff.
Parses import statements and maps common aliases to package names.
Chooses package manager commands from manifests such as package.json, pyproject.toml, requirements.txt, Cargo.toml, and go.mod.
Classifies dependencies as production or development using file paths, package patterns, and cookbook rules.
Can trigger documentation audit steps after adding new libraries.
Reports added dependencies, updated manifests, and no-change results.
limitations: It relies on import parsing and may miss dynamic or conditional imports.
It can infer the wrong package when an import name differs from the registry package.
It does not replace human review of new third-party packages.
Automatic installation can change lockfiles and run package manager behavior.

use_cases.title: Keep Backend Manifests Current
use_cases.description: Detect new Python imports after API work and update pyproject.toml or requirements.txt with the right dependency group.

use_cases.title: Update Frontend Packages After Features
use_cases.description: Map new React or TypeScript imports to npm package names and place tooling packages in devDependencies.

use_cases.title: Add Test Dependencies Correctly
use_cases.description: Identify test-only imports and classify frameworks, fixtures, and type packages as development dependencies.

prompt_templates.title: Sync Missing Imports
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the files I changed, identify new imports, and update the correct dependency manifest. Ask before installing any package.

prompt_templates.title: Classify Dependency Type
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether each new dependency belongs in production or development dependencies. Explain the placement before making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Multi-Language Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan my Python, Node.js, Go, and Rust changes for new imports. Use the matching package manager for each manifest.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Before Installing
prompt_templates.prompt: Produce a dry-run plan that maps imports to packages, shows exact commands, flags supply-chain risks, and waits for approval.

best_practices: Run in dry-run mode or ask for approval before installing packages.
Review resolved package names for typosquatting and dependency confusion risk.
Run tests and inspect manifest and lockfile diffs after changes.
anti_patterns: Do not auto-install packages from unreviewed imports in untrusted code.
Do not assume import names always match registry package names.
Do not commit manifest or lockfile changes before a human reviews the diff.

faq.question: Does this skill install dependencies automatically?
faq.answer: It is designed to install missing dependencies, but sensitive repositories should require approval before installation.

faq.question: Which ecosystems does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers Python, Node.js, Rust, Go, and Flutter workflows through common manifest files.

faq.question: Can it separate production and development dependencies?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses file paths, known package patterns, and cookbook rules to classify dependency type.

faq.question: Does it verify package safety?
faq.answer: It can check names and manifests, but it does not replace security review of third-party packages.

faq.question: Can it update documentation after adding libraries?
faq.answer: Yes. It can trigger a documentation audit step when new dependencies are added.

faq.question: What should I review after it runs?
faq.answer: Review the resolved package names, manifest changes, lockfile changes, and test results.
